hints: Focus on what makes addition polymerisation different from condensation, look only at the C=C double bond in monomer Z.
The $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-$ part must open up to become $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}-$ with only single bonds in the backbone.
Check that the whole ester side chain $-\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ stays completely unchanged and just hangs off the chain.
walkthrough:
**Spot the monomer type**

Monomer Z is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. This is an alkene with an ester side chain.

For addition polymers, only the C=C double bond reacts. Nothing is lost.

**Open the double bond**

Think of the $\pi$ bond breaking to make two new single bonds to neighbours.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}- \rightarrow -\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}-$$
The backbone becomes saturated, so no C=C remains in the polymer.

**Keep the side chain intact**

The $-\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ group does not take part. It just becomes a pendant group on every second carbon.

$$n\,\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow -[\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)]_n-$$
That matches the structure with a $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}-$ backbone and the full ester below.

options.A: Incorrect. It keeps $\text{CH}=\text{CH}$ in the backbone and loses the $-\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ part. Addition does not leave a double bond in the main chain.
options.B: Incorrect. It keeps $\text{CH}=\text{CH}$ and breaks the ester into $-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{O}-$ in the backbone. That looks like a condensation polyester idea, not addition of this alkene.
options.C: Incorrect. It shows $\text{CH}=\text{C}$ with the $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ moved. The double bond must be gone and the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ of the ester must stay as $\text{C}=\text{O}$, not become $\text{C}=\text{C}$.
options.D: Correct. The backbone is $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}-$ with only single bonds, and each $\text{CH}$ carries the unchanged $-\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ side chain. This is exactly what you get when the $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-$ double bond opens in addition polymerisation.
